title: Dear WNBA media, please stop telling fans to stick to basketball when the drama is what sells
excerpt:
OutKick WNBA reporter Dan Zaksheske discusses covering the 2026 Finals and why the league is more about drama than basketball.

During a recent episode of OutKick’s "Don’t @ Me with Dan Dakich," Dakic...
body_text:
OutKick WNBA reporter Dan Zaksheske discusses covering the 2026 Finals and why the league is more about drama than basketball.

During a recent episode of OutKick’s "Don’t @ Me with Dan Dakich," Dakich asked me, "What will be the biggest storyline in the WNBA this season, and will it have anything to do with basketball?"

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

ANGEL REESE’S WNBA FINALS SHOWED HOW CRITICISM OF HER PLAY BECOMES AN ACCUSATION OF RACISM

And believe me, I care. I just spent over two weeks flying between San Francisco and Atlanta to cover the WNBA Finals. Who won was almost beside the point for me. I was there to ask why both teams were leaving the court before the national anthem and to hear what the players, coaches and the league had to say about it.

In July, ESPN’s Chiney Ogwumike went on "First Take" and called for a reset in how the media covers Caitlin Clark and the WNBA. "In my opinion, we should be giving airtime to the beautiful basketball being played in the 30th year of the WNBA," she said.

As for that beautiful basketball, are you sure that's where you want our attention?

Gabby Williams and Angel Reese entered Game 7 as co-favorites to win WNBA Finals MVP. Through six games, the two had combined to shoot 34.4% from the field. For context, the lowest field goal percentage ever recorded by an NBA Finals MVP was Kobe Bryant's 40.5% in 2010.

At halftime of Game 7, Atlanta led 30–24. That’s 54 points on 31.8% shooting between the two teams. Reese and Williams combined for seven points on 3-for-8 shooting, with five from Reese and two from Williams.

WHY ISN’T ANGEL REESE HELD TO THE CAITLIN CLARK STANDARD WHEN FANS ATTACK HER TEAMMATES?

Then Williams scored 28 points in the second half as Golden State beat Atlanta 68–63 to win its first WNBA championship. She hit the go-ahead three with under three minutes left, finished with 30 points and four blocks, and deserved the trophy. She also shot 32.6% for the series, the lowest field goal percentage by a WNBA Finals MVP.

Atlanta Dream forward Angel Reese shot 41% from the field in the Finals, including 42% in the paint. (Peter Forest/Sipa USA via Reuters Connect)

Reese shot 40.5% from the field in the Finals, including 41.8% in the paint. She missed 28 of her 53 layups. She averaged nearly 13 rebounds, which is one reason you keep her on the floor. You’d still like your 6-foot-4 forward to make a few more shots around the basket.

Is that the basketball that you want us to talk more about, WNBA media?

After Game 3, Reese taunted Golden State with the "too small" gesture, then smiled and waved as the Valkyries walked off the court. She’d just put up 21 points and 12 rebounds, Atlanta was up 2–1, and Reese claimed that she was getting inside the Valkyries’ heads.

She proceeded to shoot 4-for-20 over the next two games and started complaining about the officiating. By Game 6, the player who’d called Golden State too small was one loss from going home.

Atlanta Dream forward Angel Reese taunts her opponents with a "too small" gesture during the 2026 WNBA playoffs. (Getty Images)

We’d seen this with Reese before. In the closing moments of the 2023 national championship game, Angel Reese followed Caitlin Clark around the court, taunting her with the "you can’t see me" gesture and pointing to her ring finger. A year later, 12.3 million people watched Clark's Iowa Hawkeyes eliminate Reese's LSU Tigers in the Elite Eight.

This August, Clark’s Fever and Reese’s Dream drew 2.6 million viewers, ESPN’s biggest WNBA audience ever. Clark is the biggest draw in women’s basketball. Put Reese on the other side and you’ve got a rivalry people have been arguing about since they were in college.

OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD

The WNBA reported 3.3 million viewers for Game 7. That’s a great number for the league (although it deserves the context that I provided in a recent column). If you tuned in to root against Angel Reese, you still got to watch Gabby Williams take over a championship game.

If you want more people to watch, quit telling them what they’re supposed to care about.

title: House Republicans sidestep effort to impeach Hegseth
excerpt: The House voted Tuesday evening to send the proposed impeachment articles against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth to the House Judiciary Committee, effectively quashing an effort to oust Hegseth from h...
body_text:
The House voted Tuesday evening to send the proposed impeachment articles against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth to the House Judiciary Committee, effectively quashing an effort to oust Hegseth from his cabinet post.

In a 211 to 204 vote, House Republicans sidestepped an effort proposed by Republican Rep. Thomas Massie of Kentucky to impeach Hegseth. Massie charged that Hegseth was negligent and conducted illegal activity in his handling of counternarcotics operations and extrajudicial killings in the Caribbean and Pacific; attacking Iran in February without congressional approval; retaliating against Sen. Mark Kelly, D-Ariz., for the veteran lawmaker’s statements to troops on illegal orders; capturing Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro without a declaration of war; and other operations.

“Secretary of Defense Peter Hegseth, by such conduct, has demonstrated that he will remain a threat to the Constitution if allowed to remain in office, and has acted in a manner grossly incompatible with his duties and the rule of law,” the articles stated.

The decision to send the articles to the Judiciary Committee likely delays the vote until January, when Democrats take over the majority in Congress.

As of Thursday, Democrats won 256 seats in the House to the Republicans’ 168, while in the Senate, Democrats have at least 54 seats to 44 Republican seats.

If the House votes to impeach Hegseth next year, a two-thirds majority would be needed on any of the articles to force Hegseth out of office.

In a rare news conference Tuesday morning before the vote, Hegseth called Massie a “disgruntled and defeated congressman” seeking to “do damage to this president, this country, and most irresponsibly, the warriors who defend it.”

Noting that President Donald Trump was impeached twice but not convicted, Hegseth said he would “take that company every day of the week.”

“These resolutions are a farce. They mock the Constitution. They attack the chain of command, and they criminalize the warfighters who execute lawful orders,” Hegseth said.

Trump has said he would stand by his defense secretary, saying Monday that he’s “done a very good job.”

If the effort had succeeded, it would have marked the second impeachment of a U.S. defense secretary and third of a cabinet member. In 2024, Homeland Security Secretary Alejandro Mayorkas was impeached over President Joe Biden’s immigration policies at the U.S.-Mexico border. The Senate voted to dismiss the charges before it went to trial.

Secretary of War William Belknap was impeached in 1876 on corruption charges shortly after he resigned. He was later acquitted in the Senate.

A survey released in October by the military-veterans advocacy non-profit Common Defense found that troops and family members are uncomfortable with what they see as the politicization of the armed forces.

According to the survey, conducted by Change Research, 54% of active-duty personnel surveyed disapproved of Hegseth, while 64% of military family members disapproved.

A majority of the group of 731 active-duty troops, veterans and military family members also believe decisions within the department were being made for political gain, and 53% of active-duty personnel said the politicization was making them want to leave the military sooner than anticipated.

Nearly half the active-duty personnel also said they oppose Operation Epic Fury, the United States’ operation against Iran.

Patricia Kime is a senior writer covering military and veterans health care, medicine and personnel issues.

title: Nick Foles believes Bears are team to beat in loaded NFC North: 'Something's brewing in Chicago'

body_text:
Nick Foles, the former Super Bowl-winning quarterback, believes his old Chicago Bears squad has "something brewing" to the point where he sees them being the team to beat in the loaded NFC North division.

The NFL trade deadline has passed, contenders have bolstered their rosters, and now the mad dash to the playoffs truly begins as we head into Week 10.

Looking around the league, the NFC North has cemented itself as the best division in football. If the regular season ended today, all four teams would be in the playoffs, though there can only be one division winner.

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

Super Bowl-winning quarterback Nick Foles knows all about the battles that occur in the NFC North year after year, and OutKick asked him who he believes will come out on top in the division during a recent interview.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Caleb Williams of the Chicago Bears warms up before the game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Soldier Field on Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026, in Chicago, Ill. (Getty Images)

He didn’t say so specifically, but one of his former teams during his playing days is standing out right now. They also happen to be atop the division at 7-2.

"There’s something brewing in Chicago, even [Monday] night with, what was it, four interceptions or something? Caleb [Williams’] still slinging it. They’re playing and making plays. [Head coach] Ben Johnson is steady, calm, cool and collected. I think the big thing, too, is if anything happens in the game, watch how he handles the referees. He really doesn’t even mess with them — he’s on to the next one. He’s just locked in, and as players, you look at your head coach and how he responds.

"So, I look at that and say, ‘Man, this team is going to stay locked in. Calm, cool and collected.’"

The Bears are riding high on a four-game win streak, but have barely set themselves apart in the division because the Detroit Lions and Minnesota Vikings are 6-2, followed by a very good Green Bay Packers squad at 6-3.

But Foles sees something in the Bears this season that is different than when he was even there.

"Chicago’s always struggled with an explosive type of offense. They’ve always been a defensive, run-first-type of team. It’s different, man," he said. "Defense is locked in. Dennis Allen is holding it down. Offense is just how many points are they going to score? They can go off at any time, even if you throw four interceptions. They’re still so dangerous."

Chicago Bears head coach Ben Johnson talks to Gervon Dexter Sr. before an NFL wild-card playoff football game against the Green Bay Packers Saturday, Jan. 10, 2026, in Chicago. (AP Photo/Nam Huh)

Foles, though, doesn’t want to discredit the rest of the teams in the division, especially the Vikings with an amazing defensive unit that makes them very scary down the stretch. They also just traded for quarterback Kirk Cousins a day after OutKick interviewed Foles.

"Minnesota Vikings defense, Brian Flores with what he’s doing there — it’s outstanding. Their offense will be their downfall — not doing anything really," Foles said. "I love the Green Bay Packers and how they’re playing right now. And Dan Campbell figuring it out with the Detroit Lions. That tenacity, the offense playing some good ball."

The best part about the NFC North: these teams have to face each other at least one more time. Those will be pivotal division matchups, as all four teams are gunning for a playoff spot.

But as we see in the playoff picture, there is a world where all of them come out of the NFC North and secure a berth to play for the Vince Lombardi Trophy. Only one team will have the home playoff game, though, with a chance to be home throughout the playoffs if things keep tracking.

Just as he did for the inaugural Australia game, Foles will be on the Netflix panel alongside Packers legend Clay Matthews, Pro Football Hall of Famer Michael Irvin and Elle Duncan.

title: French far-right author Zemmour launches second presidential bid
excerpt:
French far-right Eric Zemmour, known for his anti-Islam and anti-immigrant stance, says he’ll be standing in next year’s presidential election.

“I can confirm to you that I will indeed be ⁠a candidat...
body_text:
French far-right Eric Zemmour, known for his anti-Islam and anti-immigrant stance, says he’ll be standing in next year’s presidential election.

“I can confirm to you that I will indeed be ⁠a candidate in the presidential election”, Zemmour told TF1 TV, adding that he was running to “keep a France that is French”.

Zemmour, a 68-year-old Jewish author and veteran television commentator, finished fourth in the 2022 presidential election.

This time, he says he wants to expel foreign offenders who are in prison, as well as “foreign unemployed people who have been out of work for more than six months”, even if they are legal residents.

He says he wants “two million fewer immigrants” in France, who are seen by many among the far right as key instigators of violence during last month’s student-led cost of living protests.

Last month’s violence has led to the soaring popularity of frontrunner Marine Le Pen, with whom Zemmour will be competing against in April 2027.

Le Pen, who is the leader of the far-right National Rally party, is widely projected to win the election to replace Emmanuel Macron, who will end his term as president of France.

Meanwhile, far-left candidate Jean-Luc Melenchon of the France Unbowed party, who has been accused of encouraging the unrest, unveiled his programme on Saturday to some 17,000 supporters.

title: House GOP leaders block Massie's Hegseth impeachment push
excerpt: Hewitt argues that Massie's impeachment effort is politically motivated and intended to attract attention as he faces uncertainty over his political future, questioning the congressman's intentions an...
body_text:
Hewitt argues that Massie's impeachment effort is politically motivated and intended to attract attention as he faces uncertainty over his political future, questioning the congressman's intentions and the timing of his actions.

Secretary of War Pete Hegseth is safe from an impeachment vote in the House of Representatives after GOP leaders successfully stopped a looming vote led by Rep. Thomas Massie, R-Ky.

A vote to refer Massie's resolution to the House Judiciary Committee for consideration — which effectively killed it in its tracks — passed on Tuesday evening by a 211-204 margin, averting a potential impeachment vote on Wednesday.

President Donald Trump celebrated the failed impeachment effort in a Truth Social post, calling Massie a "major LOSER" and praising Hegseth's record on military operations in Venezuela and Iran and recruitment.

HEGSETH IMPEACHMENT VOTE LOOMS AS HOUSE REPUBLICANS PRIVATELY WARN IT COULD PASS

U.S. Secretary of War Pete Hegseth speaks during a news conference at the Pentagon on Nov. 10, 2026 in Arlington, Virginia. (Chip Somodevilla/Getty Images)

"The Democrats’ attempt to impeach Secretary of War Pete Hegseth has miserably FAILED!" Trump wrote, calling the outcome the "EXONERATION of a Great American Patriot."

The GOP had been worried about having a significant number of absences on their side after their brutal midterm election performance last week, but it appears Speaker Mike Johnson, R-La., wrangled one more victory on his way out the leadership door.

Massie's resolution is a wide-ranging piece of legislation accusing Hegseth of misusing his office via eight impeachment articles, spanning issues including the Iran war, U.S. strikes on suspected drug boats in the Caribbean and his retaliation against Sen. Mark Kelly, D-Ariz., over a video calling on troops to disobey "unlawful orders."

Hegseth railed against the effort and criticized Massie personally during a news conference Tuesday morning.

HEGSETH LABELS IMPEACHMENT PUSH A POLICY DISPUTE, BUT DO LAWMAKERS' ALLEGATIONS RISE TO HIGH CRIMES?

"What one disgruntled and defeated congressman is attempting is not oversight, and it's not accountability. It's a political spectacle, a personal manifesto driven by ego and resentment," Hegseth said.

The outgoing Kentucky Republican was able to force Tuesday night's vote over the objections of House GOP leaders by filing a privileged resolution, a mechanism aimed at bypassing the will of the chamber's majority. A privileged resolution must be considered within two legislative days of being filed.

Rep. Thomas Massie, R-Ky., speaks on impeaching U.S. Secretary of War Pete Hegseth outside the U.S. Capitol on Nov. 9, 2026 in Washington, D.C. (Andrew Harnik/Getty Images)

REPORTER'S NOTEBOOK: HOW MIDTERMS MAY CHANGE THE HOUSE IMPEACHMENT EQUATION FOR HEGSETH

All Democrats present backed moving forward with the impeachment on Tuesday evening, as expected. All Republicans but Massie voted to kill the resolution.

But some were worried earlier in the day about weak attendance potentially clearing the path for an actual impeachment vote.

"I'm going to vote no," Rep. Jake Ellzey, R-Texas, told Fox News Digital. "I don't know if any Republicans other than Massie will be in support of his articles of impeachment, but I don't even know how many Republicans will be here by the time of the vote. The real question is how short are we. Numerically, if they're all here and we're not, what happens then?"

Ellzey called the impeachment effort "a ridiculous waste of time."

Even House Republicans who are critical of Hegseth were hesitant to support Massie's resolution.

"I think it's an effort to scapegoat Pete Hegseth for Congress shirking their own duty and, frankly, the president taking action that, in my view, is unconstitutional. but it's also not unprecedented," Rep. Warren Davidson, R-Ohio, who is opposed to the Trump administration's involvement in Iran, said.

Rep. Warren Davidson, R-Ohio, leaves the House Republican Conference caucus meeting at the Capitol Hill Club in Washington on Wednesday, May 13, 2026. (Bill Clark/CQ-Roll Call, Inc via Getty Images)

"What would be unprecedented is to hold the secretary of defense accountable for a decision the president makes. Or, frankly, it would have been unprecedented for the secretary of defense to kind of break ranks on something that is clearly not unprecedented in terms of what has become the standard operating procedure for administrations going back to the Korean War."

Rep. Don Bacon, R-Neb., a vocal critic of Hegseth's, told reporters Tuesday, "I'm personally not a fan of the secretary. I don't think he was the right guy in the job. But, also, when you read Massie's impeachment, I don't agree with it."

Elizabeth Elkind is a politics reporter for Fox News Digital leading coverage of the House of Representatives. Previous digital bylines seen at Daily Mail and CBS News.

title: Former Seattle Mariners player Dave Edler critically injured in Yakima crash that killed his wife
excerpt: A 26-year-old Washington man faces felony charges after a deadly head-on crash Sunday afternoon killed the wife of former Seattle Mariners player and Yakima mayor Dave Edler, leaving the former big le...
body_text:
A 26-year-old Washington man faces felony charges after a deadly head-on crash Sunday afternoon killed the wife of former Seattle Mariners player and Yakima mayor Dave Edler, leaving the former big leaguer critically injured.

Brad Wellman slides into base as third baseman Dave Edler drops the throw in the fourth inning during a Denver Bears baseball game. (Denver Post via Getty Images)

According to the Yakima Police Department, the collision occurred around 4:30 p.m. in the 7600 block of Coolidge Road near South 76th Avenue.

Investigators stated that an oncoming vehicle traveling westbound at high speed crossed the center line into the eastbound lane, slamming into the Edlers' car. Emergency responders had to cut both victims from the crushed wreckage. Susie Edler, 67, and Dave Edler, 70, were rushed to MultiCare Yakima Memorial Hospital with catastrophic injuries.

A Seattle Mariners batting helmet is seen during a game against the Arizona Diamondbacks at T-Mobile Park in Seattle, Wash., on Sept. 10, 2021. (Getty Images)

Susie Edler died shortly after arriving. Dave Edler was stabilized and airlifted to Harborview Medical Center in Seattle, where he remains in critical condition.

Authorities identified the driver of the other vehicle as 26-year-old Trevor Allen Stockton of Yakima.

Law enforcement stated that alcohol impairment is suspected to have been a direct factor in the wreck.

ICE LODGES DETAINER FOR ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT CHARGED IN WRONG-WAY MARYLAND CRASH THAT KILLED MOM, DAUGHTER

Officers took Stockton into custody at the scene, and prosecutors formally charged him with vehicular homicide and vehicular assault.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Stockton made his preliminary court appearance Monday in Yakima County Superior Court. The presiding judge set bail at $75,000, calling attention during the proceedings to what was described as Stockton's cold reaction following the crash.

A Seattle Mariners batting helmet is shown during the game between the Toronto Blue Jays and the Seattle Mariners at T-Mobile Park on Sunday, May 11, 2025, in Seattle, Wash. (MLB Photos via Getty Images)

Dave Edler remains a prominent figure in central Washington sports and the local community.

After playing college baseball at Washington State University, the Seattle Mariners selected him in 1978, and he played 126 games for the franchise between 1980 and 1983.

Following his baseball career, Edler entered public life, serving on the Yakima City Council from 2003 to 2006 before serving a term as mayor from 2006 to 2010. He and his wife also served as pastoral leaders at Yakima Foursquare Church for three decades. Investigators are still awaiting official toxicology results as they wrap up the case.

title: Nvidia hires major US law firm to investigate alleged Chinese spy affair
excerpt:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has become the face of the US AI boom

Nvidia has hired one of the largest law firms in the US to investigate the affair between its own chief executive and an alleged Chinese ...
body_text:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has become the face of the US AI boom

Nvidia has hired one of the largest law firms in the US to investigate the affair between its own chief executive and an alleged Chinese spy.

Jensen Huang, who co-founded the tech company, has admitted to having a romantic relationship outside of his marriage. The woman, Alice Huang, is alleged to be a spy for Beijing.

Nvidia said on Tuesday that it had hired New York law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz, and that its attorney Joon Kim would lead "a thorough and independent investigation". The FBI is also conducting its own probe.

The company's share price has fallen almost to a yearly low, with $500bn (£375bn) wiped of its stock market value since Friday.

Nvidia is widely considered one of the most important companies behind the artificial intelligence (AI) boom, given it is the sole manufacturer of a computer chip used in AI tools.

It is the world's second most valuable company after Apple and its chips have become a matter of national security for US officials who are keen to win the AI race.

Alice Huang, who is also known as Huang Le, and is not related to Jensen Huang, was an executive at Singaporean company Megaspeed, which has been a customer of Nvidia.

Megaspeed had been suspected of helping divert Nvidia chips to China, a concern that Nvidia has said was investigated and debunked.

Nvidia has also maintained that the US government did not inform it that Megaspeed posed an intelligence concern.

What we know so far about Jensen Huang's affair with suspected Chinese spy

Zoe Kleinman: Nvidia CEO's affair will cause ripples across US and beyond

According to the New York Times, Secretary of State Marco Rubio sent a memo to top officials in Washington earlier this year warning that Jensen Huang was in a close relationship with a Chinese spy.

Beijing has rejected claims that the Nvidia chief has been targeted, with its foreign ministry saying the allegations were "intended to smear and malign China".

US President Donald Trump said on Monday that he had spoken to Jensen Huang, who had said he had "no idea she was a spy." Trump said he believed him.

However, the relationship has drawn more political attention. Congressional leaders of the House Committee on Foreign Affairs have asked Huang to appear next week for a closed door briefing.

The Nvidia boss has yet to say whether he will attend, a person familiar with the committee's demand told the BBC. The committee has the authority to subpoena Huang, effectively forcing him to appear before it, if deemed necessary.

When announcing on Sunday that it would investigate the affair, Nvidia's board said it had no reason to believe the company's secrets or national security were compromised.

It added that a committee of independent directors would oversee the probe.

Watch: Who is suspected Chinese spy at centre of Nvidia affair investigation?

Wachtell is one of the largest law firms in the US and has several notable clients in the tech industry. Among them are OpenAI and Salesforce.

Joon Kim is a former US Attorney for New York's Southern District and spent several years working as a government attorney focusing on fraud and other criminal acts.

The Nvidia investigation will likely be treated as urgent, according to sources familiar with the matter, as Jensen Huang's public image is tightly intertwined with the company.

He has become a key public figure in the development on AI, arguing the technology is a "new industrial revolution" and is on par with the advent of electricity.

It is unclear, however, if Wachtell will be able to interview Alice Huang.

A spokesperson for Nvidia declined to comment on Tuesday when asked if Jensen Huang had retained any of his own legal representation amid the company investigation and the separate one launched by the FBI.

Here are the winners and losers of the 2026 NFL trade deadline:

While a 38-year-old Kirk Cousins is hardly glamorous, he's considerably better than Carson Wentz, Kyler Murray or any other realistic option the Vikings had.

He's also still an above-average quarterback, currently second in the NFL in passing touchdowns.

BOBBY BURACK: DIANNA RUSSINI WANTS SYMPATHY WITHOUT ACCOUNTABILITY IN MIKE VRABEL SCANDAL

Kirk Cousins celebrates on the field after the Minnesota Vikings defeated the Indianapolis Colts at U.S. Bank Stadium in Minneapolis, Minn., on Dec. 17, 2022. (Getty Images)

The Chargers appear determined to become the first team to start 0-8 and make the playoffs. Either that, or they're the biggest losers of the entire deadline.

The reports were true. The Chargers held on to veterans with expiring contracts, including Khalil Mack and Donte Jackson, both of whom could have fetched solid draft capital in return.

The team did, however, trade its homegrown, emerging linebacker Daiyan Henley – to the division rival Denver Broncos.

The Bears were quiet on deadline day because they made their move two weeks ago. No team improved more through a trade this season than Chicago did by acquiring All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons.

Simmons has made an immediate impact in Chicago, improving the play of the defenders around him, notably Devin Bush and Austin Booker.

Most sportsbooks have moved the Bears from 10th to third in Super Bowl odds in recent weeks. Trading for Simmons is part of the reason.

Chicago Bears defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons (99) leaves the field after the Bears defeated the Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field in Seattle, Wash., on Nov. 2, 2026. (IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect)

Jacksonville sent the Eagles a 2027 first-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick for Davis. He is a good player, but primarily a run-stuffing nose tackle. The Jaguars paid as if he were a difference-making pass rusher. He isn't.

They also sent Atlanta a 2027 second-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick for Bates. The problem: Bates is a free agent after the season, and the Jaguars are projected to be over the salary cap.

What's more, the Bills acquired fellow safety Amani Hooker at a much better price. Buffalo sent Tennessee a second-round pick and received a fifth-round pick along with Hooker. He's also two years younger than Bates and has two and a half years remaining on his contract.

Russini returned to media just in time for the trade deadline. She posted her first tweet since April, confirming that the 49ers were not trading Mac Jones.

But her inactivity isn't what lands her on the losers list. It's how she portrayed herself in her first interview since resigning from The Athletic following the scandal involving Mike Vrabel.

In an interview with People, Russini claimed she is the victim of "heartbreaking" lies and took no accountability for her role in the scandal.

Former NFL quarterback Nick Foles gave his take on his old Indianapolis Colts teammates, running back Jonathan Taylor, and whether his ex-team should trade him before the NFL deadline on Nov. 10.

The NFL trade deadline came and went Tuesday afternoon and the Indianapolis Colts underperformed – kind of like they've been doing on the field this season.

The Colts were offered multiple trades for running back Jonathan Taylor in the last week, league sources told OutKick and Fox News Digital, adding that several of those offers included multiple picks and even high draft picks.

But the Colts were intent on getting some sort of blockbuster deal for Taylor.

And they did not get that, so they did not trade Taylor.

The Colts also engaged in conversations with at least one other team (the Minnesota Vikings, one source said) about Daniel Jones but kept their embattled starting quarterback.

MORE PROOF THAT ANY TEAM TRADING FOR DANIEL JONES AT THE NFL TRADE DEADLINE IS CHASING FOOL'S GOLD

The Colts did, however, trade a pair of solid but not outstanding receivers in Josh Downs and Keenan Allen.

COLTS GM CHRIS BALLARD ON KEENAN ALLEN DUI ARREST: 'HE'S A TREMENDOUS HUMAN BEING. GIVE HIM SOME GRACE'

The Colts added a fourth- and fifth-round pick for Downs in their trade with the Kansas City Chiefs. The Colts also added a sixth-round pick in 2027 from the San Francisco 49ers for Allen.

Indianapolis Colts wide receiver Keenan Allen runs through a drill during a joint training camp practice with the Atlanta Falcons on Aug. 20, 2026, at Grand Park Sports Campus in Westfield, Ind. (Icon Sportswire via Getty Images)

Both Downs and Allen moving on make sense in that Downs asked to be traded a couple of weeks ago, Allen is 34 years old, and both are playing on expiring contracts.

COLTS TRADE PRO BOWL GUARD QUENTON NELSON TO SEAHAWKS, THE FIRST OF WHAT COULD BE MULTIPLE DEADLINE MOVES

But it's the stuff the Colts failed to do that raises eyebrows.

They had a trade for Taylor in the offing the last week or so. Fox Sports reported that offer was from the New York Giants and would have brought a second-round and fifth-round pick for Taylor.

Jonathan Taylor No. 28 of the Indianapolis Colts reacts after a 24-yard touchdown run late in the second quarter of an NFL game against the Kansas City Chiefs on Sept. 20, 2026, at Arrowhead Stadium in Kansas City, Mo. (Icon Sportswire via Getty Images)

JONATHAN TAYLOR DELIVERS WHAT SOUNDS LIKE A GOODBYE TO INDIANAPOLIS AFTER COLTS' FIFTH STRAIGHT LOSS

And they decided not to pull the trigger.

That trade would have sent the Colts a package somewhat similar to one the San Francisco 49ers gave up for Christian McCaffrey, but as the Colts considered the offer, the Giants pulled it. The Colts wanted a deal that included more picks or a higher pick than the No. 2 selection.

Yes, the Colts wanted a No. 1 pick for Taylor.

And no one offered that, so the club informed Taylor he wasn't being traded. The same with Jones as he seemed to know by early Tuesday afternoon that he was not going to be traded.

The Colts had other opportunities to make trades to increase their future draft capital but apparently dithered.

A league source told OutKick and Fox News Digital that the Colts could have traded starting defensive tackle Grover Stewart for a fifth-round pick. The offer was upgraded to a fourth-round pick and another late-round pick.

But as the Colts waited to get an even better offer, all offers were pulled.

The messaging the Colts apparently put out through various media outlets after Tuesday's trade deadline anticlimax surrounding Taylor is simply astounding: They didn't want have a garage sale that could potentially hurt their ability to hire a top general manager or perhaps head coach if current coach Shane Steichen is fired after this season.

They kept Taylor and Jones to use them as a lure for a future executive or coach.

That, by the way, is ridiculous reasoning.

The Colts wanted to keep two players that haven't been able to lift the current team above its 2-7 record as a way of somehow convincing a future unidentified GM or head coach to work in Indy.

That is illogical because a future GM or coach might want the use of more draft picks to build their team in whatever image they wish rather than inheriting players currently on the team.

And this: It is quite possible that after spending the last couple of weeks on trade watch, and delivering what sounded like a farewell message following Sunday's loss to the Dallas Cowboys, Taylor might be disappointed he's still on a losing team instead of headed to a team that wanted him for a postseason push.

The Colts have been a grand disappointment this season.

And their work leading right up to the NFL trade deadline was more of the same.

title: Republicans elect Jim Jordan as House minority leader after midterm defeats
excerpt:
Republicans pick Jordan as House leader and John Thune as Senate leader for last two years of Trump’s presidency

Republicans have elected veteran congressman Jim Jordan as their new leader in the Hou...
body_text:
Republicans pick Jordan as House leader and John Thune as Senate leader for last two years of Trump’s presidency

Republicans have elected veteran congressman Jim Jordan as their new leader in the House of Representatives, putting a strident defender of Donald Trump at the helm of their conference as they navigate the fallout from sweeping losses in last week’s midterm elections.

Jordan will serve as minority leader under the new Congress that begins next year, where Democrats will have their largest margins in both the House and Senate in years. He will be responsible for shaping the party’s strategy against the waves of investigations Democrats have promised to open into Trump’s second administration, as well as their vows of an ambitious legislative agenda, regardless of whether it has the president’s support.

“Over the next two years, House Republicans will fight for American families,” Jordan said in brief remarks to reporters after his elections. “When Democrats offer more government, we’ll offer more freedom, and we will bring that fight in committee, on the floor, and on the stump every single day.”

The Ohio lawmaker is a longtime leader of the right wing in the US House, and gained national renown for standing up for Trump against earlier efforts by Democrats to hold him to account. In 2023, Jordan was briefly a candidate for speaker after dissident Republicans removed Kevin McCarthy as the chamber’s leader, but his bid collapsed after it became clear he did not have enough support.

House Republicans elected Jordan over Steve Scalise, who serves as majority leader in the current Congress. Following comprehensive defeats last week in the midterm elections, the current House speaker, Mike Johnson, announced he would not remain in leadership, and has thus far not committed to serving out the rest of his term.

“Jim was a mentor of mine when I first came to Congress 10 years ago, and we worked alongside one another all these years,” Johnson said. “He’s always been regarded as a leader by the conference, and he’s going to do an extraordinary job.”

Jordan will serve alongside John Thune, the Republican Senate leader who also won re-election from his conference on Tuesday.

“I’m proud of what this Republican team has accomplished together, and we remain united in our commitment to advancing conservative priorities, working with President Trump and our colleagues in the House, and holding the line against Democrats’ efforts to enact their far-left, liberal agenda,” Thune said in a statement.

Elections for both roles were held in behind-closed-door meetings.

Ahead of the House GOP’s meeting, several spoke of the need for a change in strategy, after two years spent trying to answer Trump’s demands with one of the smallest majorities in history, only to have voters decisively remove them from power.

“I want somebody that’s going to message and admit that … we made mistakes,” said Tim Burchett, a conservative lawmaker from Tennessee, who declined to say who he would be voting for.

Florida congresswoman Anna Paulina Luna said she was backing Jordan, and blamed Scalise for not fighting hard enough to get rightwing priorities through the chamber.

“If you have a play and you get destroyed, you don’t put the same people back in charge that were part of running that failed play,” she said.

First elected in 2006, Jordan helped found the rightwing House Freedom Caucus in 2015, and served as its first chair. Seen almost always in shirtsleeves, his profile rose during Trump’s first term, particularly after Democrats regained control of Congress’s lower chamber in the 2018 midterms. As the top Republican on the oversight and then the judiciary committees, Jordan made energetic stands against efforts by Democrats to investigate Trump, and served as a member of the president’s defense team during his first impeachment.

Jordan echoed Trump’s false claims of fraud in the 2020 election, and championed the investigation of Hunter Biden during Joe Biden’s final two years in office. Since Trump returned to the White House, Jordan has used his role as judiciary committee chair to pursue allegations of “weaponization” by prosecutors who investigated Trump, including Jack Smith, the special counsel who oversaw the federal cases.

Democrats decried Jordan’s appointment as sign that the party was doubling down on extremism, with Virginia congressman Don Beyer noting that Jordan’s election came days after Trump had named immigration hardliner Stephen Miller as his chief of staff.

“Republicans learned absolutely nothing from what happened a week ago, and are responding by elevating their most extreme voices to positions of power,” he said.

title: Russia expels Moldovan diplomat in tit-for-tat move
excerpt:
Russia has expelled a Moldovan diplomat in retaliation for Chisinau’s expulsion of a Russian embassy employee over the crash of a drone in Moldova.

Russia’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs said on Tuesda...
body_text:
Russia has expelled a Moldovan diplomat in retaliation for Chisinau’s expulsion of a Russian embassy employee over the crash of a drone in Moldova.

Russia’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs said on Tuesday that it had summoned Moldova’s ambassador, Lilian Darii, and informed him that a member of the Moldovan embassy’s staff had been declared unacceptable “on the basis of the principle of reciprocity”.

“A strong protest was lodged with the ambassador after the Moldovan authorities on October 23 declared an employee of the Russian embassy in Chisinau persona non grata,” the ministry said in a statement.

It said Moldova’s decision was made “under the formal pretext of the alleged discovery on the territory of the republic of debris of an unmanned aerial vehicle carrying explosives”, calling it “another unfriendly step”.

The ministry said the “true goal” of the move was “to further undermine the centuries-long history of Russian-Moldovan relations”.

Last month, Moldovan President Maia Sandu said a “Russian attack drone” had violated the country’s airspace and “crashed near homes and an energy facility”.

Moldova then declared a staff member of the Russian embassy “persona non grata”.

Drones have penetrated Moldovan territory on multiple occasions since Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.

Since then, Russia’s relations with former Soviet states, such as Moldova, have hit an all-time low, compounded by the push by some of those states to join the European Union.

On Sunday, Moldova officially launched a new power line connecting the country to neighbouring Romania and the European grid to reduce its dependence on Russian energy.

The 400-kilovolt extra-high-voltage line, which runs from the city of Vulcanesti to Chisinau, allows Moldova to cut reliance on the Cuciurgan thermal power plant in Transnistria.

Other European-aligned states in the Black Sea region say they are experiencing renewed attacks allegedly carried out by Moscow, such as a drone strike that sank a cargo ship off Romania’s Black Sea coast in October.

title: Thomas Markle, Meghan’s father, jailed after cutting off ankle monitor, DoJ says
excerpt:
Estranged father of Duchess of Sussex was arrested for keeping child sexual abuse material, authorities say

The estranged father of Meghan Markle, the Duchess of Sussex, has been jailed after US auth...
body_text:
Estranged father of Duchess of Sussex was arrested for keeping child sexual abuse material, authorities say

The estranged father of Meghan Markle, the Duchess of Sussex, has been jailed after US authorities said he cut an electronic monitoring device off his ankle, days after his arrest for keeping child sexual abuse material in storage units in California.

Thomas Markle, 82, was in custody awaiting a hearing in federal court in Tampa, Florida, first assistant US attorney Bill Essayli said. He was arrested shortly after he cut off the ankle bracelet at 1.45am on Tuesday, Essayli said.

“Release conditions are court orders, not suggestions. We are asking the court to revoke his release and detain him pending trial, and we will continue to prosecute this case to the fullest extent of the law,” Essayli said.

The US magistrate judge Lindsay Griffin agreed on Tuesday that Markle now must be kept in custody.

Markle’s arrest on Friday followed the seizure of approximately 78 items, including slides, film negatives and books that contained suspected child sexual abuse images in storage in the Los Angeles area, Essayli said.

Among the alleged child sexual abuse material were sexually explicit photographs of Markle with underage girls, including one taken in what appears to be part of a motel chain in the Philippines, Reuters reports.

According to the criminal complaint, the special agent investigating Markle’s alleged storage unit said he “viewed a collection of what appeared to be strips of 35mm film negatives seized from Storage Unit 1 registered to Markle”.

“To date, I have identified approximately 18 images that appeared to constitute child pornography,” the special agent noted in the complaint, adding that the investigation remains ongoing.

Markle reportedly had rented the storage units in Los Angeles since 2008, with the FBI noting that the most recent auto-payment for the units was on 14 October.

“Markle’s use of Storage Unit 1 was also corroborated by items found within the unit bearing his name, including boxes labeled ‘Tom Markle’ and an address within the central district of California,” the criminal complaint said.

During his arrest last week, he was taken from a senior care center in Lakeland, Florida, by ambulance. Hours later, a judge allowed Markle to be released on the condition that he be electronically monitored, which typically means wearing an ankle tether.

According to Griffin, Markle’s court appearance last Friday included a “lack of recall”. Griffin also cited Markle’s “health condition” and “advanced age” as part of his appearance.

The judge ordered a mental competency exam and a report by 20 November.

Griffin said she found “reasonable cause to believe” Markle was suffering from a condition “rendering him mentally incompetent to the extent that he is unable to understand the nature and consequences of the proceedings against him or to assist properly in his defense”, CBS reported.

His daughter, Meghan, the Duchess of Sussex, married Prince Harry at Windsor Castle in 2018. They have two children, Prince Archie and Princess Lilibet. She is an American citizen and actor who starred in the US television drama Suits.

Meghan recently said she was “deeply distressed” by allegations that a collection of child sexual abuse images had been found at her father’s former home. She also revealed that a letter containing “troubling allegations” about him had been sent to police in London in 2019.

“It made troubling and disturbing allegations against my father and I was given assurances that these were being investigated,” Meghan said of the letter. “I hope it can now be understood that, despite certain media publications’ distortion over the years, any distance from my father and my choice to not allow him to have contact with our children was for one reason: to protect them.”

Thomas Markle was living in the Philippines this year when he suffered a stroke and had his left leg amputated. That forced him to return to the US.

His arrest followed reports by the Sun, a British tabloid newspaper, that Meghan’s half-brother found a collection of child sexual abuse images while clearing out their father’s home in the Philippines. That discovery led to information about two US storage units in California, which Markle had rented since 2008.

title: Ilhan Omar huddles with her DC-based lawyers during her first day back on Capitol Hill amid federal probes
excerpt: Rep. Ilhan Omar, D-Minn., told Fox News she is not concerned that the federal investigations into her immigration status and financial filings will distract her from serving her constituents in Congre...
body_text:
Rep. Ilhan Omar, D-Minn., told Fox News she is not concerned that the federal investigations into her immigration status and financial filings will distract her from serving her constituents in Congress following a lengthy meeting with her lawyers.

Rep. Ilhan Omar, D-Minn., returned to Capitol Hill this week and brought two lawyers with her after a scandal-plagued fall recess.

Fox News spotted the two attorneys exiting her Washington, D.C., office Tuesday after what appeared to be a roughly two-hour meeting with the congresswoman.

Omar hired two high-profile attorneys, Amy Jeffress and Joshua Matz, both of whom are partners at Heckler Fink LLP, amid dueling investigations. After emerging from Omar’s office on Tuesday, Fox News asked about their confidence in Omar’s defense against the federal government.

OBAMA ADMIN FIRST LAUNCHED THE INVESTIGATION INTO ILHAN OMAR'S ALLEGED BROTHER MARRIAGE

The attorneys were also asked about the recent news that both the Obama and Biden administrations had been the first to investigate Omar after she claimed that the Trump administration was politically targeting her.

Rep. Ilhan Omar, D-Minn., speaks during a news conference Wednesday in which she blamed President Donald Trump for death threats and attacks against her. (AP Photo/Adam Gray)

This is the first sighting of Omar back on the Hill after two federal departments opened investigations into the Somali-born congresswoman looking into both her immigration status and previous financial filings.

In October, agents with Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) raided her Washington, D.C., home as part of what Fox News Digital learned was an investigation into whether she or her father committed fraud when filling out her immigration paperwork.

She spent the final weeks of her campaign asking for money to defend herself in the investigations and accusing Trump of targeting her for political reasons.

About an hour after Omar's lawyers exited her office Tuesday, the congresswoman departed with husband Tim Mynett.

She was approached by Fox News about the ongoing investigation and asked whether she is concerned it could affect her ability to effectively represent her constituents in Congress.

She was then asked if there was any chance she would step down from Congress despite just winning re-election to let the investigation "play out."

The congresswoman smiled and waved at the camera but did not respond as the elevator doors closed with her inside.

SCANDAL-PLAGUED ILHAN OMAR EASILY SECURES 5TH TERM IN DEEP BLUE MINNESOTA DESPITE IMMIGRATION FRAUD PROBE

Rep. Ilhan Omar, D-Minn., pictured walking and talking in the U.S. Capitol basement. (Fox News Digital)

Omar also refused to respond to Fox’s question about whether she had spoken to House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries about the investigation.

The attorneys seen exiting her office earlier, Jeffress and Matz, have both represented high-ranking Democratic elected officials and have taken on multiple cases against President Donald Trump, his allies and supporters.

Jeffress served as former President Joe Biden’s attorney in his lawsuit against the Justice Department earlier this year. She also served as counsel for then-House Speaker Nancy Pelosi and the House committee investigating the Jan. 6, 2021, riot on Capitol Hill.

She is also married to U.S. District Judge Christopher Cooper of the District of Washington, who ruled in May that Trump's addition his name to the John F. Kennedy Performing Arts Center was illegal.

ILHAN OMAR LASHES OUT AT 'BIGOT' TRUMP AFTER WINNING RE-ELECTION DESPITE INVESTIGATION

UFC CEO Dana White listens as President Donald Trump speaks in the James S. Brady Press Briefing Room at the White House in Washington, D.C., Nov. 9, 2026. (Reuters)

Matz served as counsel to House Democrats during both failed impeachment attempts against Trump during his first term in office. Matz also represented E. Jean Carroll in two civil cases against Trump’s denial of her sexual assault claims against him.

Matz also represented those opposed to the Florida Parental Rights in Education Act, which banned teachers from teaching students about gender identity and sexual orientation.

Omar has not yet formally announced a meeting with any members of Congress about the two ongoing federal probes. Her only formal address to the public on the investigations was posting to social media, including a video in which she encouraged her supporters to keep sending money in light of the new investigations against her.

Fox News Digital's Peter D'Abrosca contributed to this report.

Hannah is a Production Assistant for the Politics team at Fox News Digital.

title: Ilhan Omar huddles with her DC-based lawyers during her first day back on Capitol Hill amid federal probes
excerpt: Rep. Ilhan Omar, D-Minn., told Fox News she is not concerned that the federal investigations into her immigration status and financial filings will distract her from serving her constituents in Congre...
body_text:
Rep. Ilhan Omar, D-Minn., told Fox News she is not concerned that the federal investigations into her immigration status and financial filings will distract her from serving her constituents in Congress following a lengthy meeting with her lawyers.

Rep. Ilhan Omar, D-Minn., returned to Capitol Hill this week and brought two lawyers with her after a scandal-plagued fall recess.

Fox News spotted the two attorneys exiting her Washington, D.C., office Tuesday after what appeared to be a roughly two-hour meeting with the congresswoman.

Omar hired two high-profile attorneys, Amy Jeffress and Joshua Matz, both of whom are partners at Heckler Fink LLP, amid dueling investigations. After emerging from Omar’s office on Tuesday, Fox News asked about their confidence in Omar’s defense against the federal government.

OBAMA ADMIN FIRST LAUNCHED THE INVESTIGATION INTO ILHAN OMAR'S ALLEGED BROTHER MARRIAGE

The attorneys were also asked about the recent news that both the Obama and Biden administrations had been the first to investigate Omar after she claimed that the Trump administration was politically targeting her.

Rep. Ilhan Omar, D-Minn., speaks during a news conference Wednesday in which she blamed President Donald Trump for death threats and attacks against her. (AP Photo/Adam Gray)

This is the first sighting of Omar back on the Hill after two federal departments opened investigations into the Somali-born congresswoman looking into both her immigration status and previous financial filings.

In October, agents with Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) raided her Washington, D.C., home as part of what Fox News Digital learned was an investigation into whether she or her father committed fraud when filling out her immigration paperwork.

She spent the final weeks of her campaign asking for money to defend herself in the investigations and accusing Trump of targeting her for political reasons.

About an hour after Omar's lawyers exited her office Tuesday, the congresswoman departed with husband Tim Mynett.

She was approached by Fox News about the ongoing investigation and asked whether she is concerned it could affect her ability to effectively represent her constituents in Congress.

She was then asked if there was any chance she would step down from Congress despite just winning re-election to let the investigation "play out."

The congresswoman smiled and waved at the camera but did not respond as the elevator doors closed with her inside.

SCANDAL-PLAGUED ILHAN OMAR EASILY SECURES 5TH TERM IN DEEP BLUE MINNESOTA DESPITE IMMIGRATION FRAUD PROBE

Rep. Ilhan Omar, D-Minn., pictured walking and talking in the U.S. Capitol basement. (Fox News Digital)

Omar also refused to respond to Fox’s question about whether she had spoken to House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries about the investigation.

The attorneys seen exiting her office earlier, Jeffress and Matz, have both represented high-ranking Democratic elected officials and have taken on multiple cases against President Donald Trump, his allies and supporters.

Jeffress served as former President Joe Biden’s attorney in his lawsuit against the Justice Department earlier this year. She also served as counsel for then-House Speaker Nancy Pelosi and the House committee investigating the Jan. 6, 2021, riot on Capitol Hill.

She is also married to U.S. District Judge Christopher Cooper of the District of Washington, who ruled in May that Trump's addition his name to the John F. Kennedy Performing Arts Center was illegal.

ILHAN OMAR LASHES OUT AT 'BIGOT' TRUMP AFTER WINNING RE-ELECTION DESPITE INVESTIGATION

UFC CEO Dana White listens as President Donald Trump speaks in the James S. Brady Press Briefing Room at the White House in Washington, D.C., Nov. 9, 2026. (Reuters)

Matz served as counsel to House Democrats during both failed impeachment attempts against Trump during his first term in office. Matz also represented E. Jean Carroll in two civil cases against Trump’s denial of her sexual assault claims against him.

Matz also represented those opposed to the Florida Parental Rights in Education Act, which banned teachers from teaching students about gender identity and sexual orientation.

Omar has not yet formally announced a meeting with any members of Congress about the two ongoing federal probes. Her only formal address to the public on the investigations was posting to social media, including a video in which she encouraged her supporters to keep sending money in light of the new investigations against her.

Fox News Digital's Peter D'Abrosca contributed to this report.

Hannah is a Production Assistant for the Politics team at Fox News Digital.

title: Kirk Cousins is back in Minnesota, and the Vikings' NFC odds are still too long
excerpt: Nick Wright, Chris Broussard, Kevin Wildes, and Danny Parkins analyze some cool stats entering Week 9, including the Minnesota Vikings needing better performances from their offense, Jaxon Smith-Njigb...
body_text:
Nick Wright, Chris Broussard, Kevin Wildes, and Danny Parkins analyze some cool stats entering Week 9, including the Minnesota Vikings needing better performances from their offense, Jaxon Smith-Njigba and the Seattle Seahawks needing some help, and Joe Burrow’s MVP pace.

The league’s best scoring defense finally has a quarterback. The NFC board still has Minnesota seventh.

The Vikings spent the first half of the season trying to win with whoever was standing closest to the huddle. On Tuesday, they called an old friend.

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

Minnesota sent a 2027 third-round pick to Las Vegas for Kirk Cousins, bringing the 38-year-old back to the team he left after 2023. Cousins returns to replace his replacement, and the Super Bowl market reacted fast.

SUPER BOWL BETTING SITES 2027 — BEST SPORTSBOOKS FOR SUPER BOWL LXI

The Vikings opened the season at 50-1 to win Super Bowl LXI. After Monday’s loss to Buffalo, they slid to +3000. Hours after the trade, they’re back to +2200 to +2500 across major sportsbooks.

Halving the opening price looks like a big move. It mostly reflects a team that’s 6-2 and finally fixed its biggest problem.

Kirk Cousins of the Las Vegas Raiders leaves the field after the team's 27-14 loss to the Arizona Cardinals in a preseason game at Allegiant Stadium on Aug. 13, 2026, in Las Vegas, Nev. (Getty Images)

The Vikings’ record isn’t the story. How they got it is.

Minnesota has the league’s top scoring defense. The offense ranks 27th in points, 31st in yards and 31st in passing. The Vikings have scored 16 or fewer points in five of eight games, including each of the last three.

The quarterback room has been a mess since J.J. McCarthy was shipped to the Giants on Sept. 28. Kyler Murray is out with a hamstring injury. Carson Wentz turned it over three times in Monday’s 23-6 loss to Buffalo and got pulled for Max Brosmer. Minnesota converted 25% of its third downs that night.

A team that wins six of eight with an offense ranking 31st in EPA per play isn’t lucky. It’s a team that’s one competent quarterback away.

Nobody is confusing 38-year-old Kirk with prime Kirk, but he doesn’t need to be.

He threw for 2,340 yards, 20 touchdowns and eight interceptions on a 4-5 Raiders team that had nothing around him. Now he walks back into Kevin O’Connell’s offense, the same system where he threw for 4,547 yards and 29 touchdowns in a 13-4 season in 2022.

There’s no install period. He already knows the playbook, the play caller and the building.

Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins and Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes talk on the field after an NFL football game in Las Vegas on Sunday, Oct. 4, 2026. (AP Photo/John Locher)

The Super Bowl number moved. The NFC number still has Minnesota seventh, behind two division rivals and a Seattle team priced right next to Green Bay.

The honest problem is the division. At 6-2, Minnesota is third in the NFC North, and the Bears are priced as the second-best team in the conference. That’s why the division bet doesn’t interest me, but the conference price does.

The Vikings don’t need to win the North to make a run. They’re -250 to make the playoffs, and once they’re in, the best scoring defense in football with a veteran quarterback is a nightmare draw in January.

Kirk Cousins celebrates on the field after the Minnesota Vikings defeated the Indianapolis Colts at U.S. Bank Stadium in Minneapolis, Minn., on Dec. 17, 2022. (Getty Images)

The Super Bowl price ranges from +2200 to +2500 depending on the book, and that gap is real money on a futures ticket. Line-shop before you bet.

You also get an immediate test. Cousins could debut Sunday at Lambeau, where the Vikings are 3.5-point underdogs against the Packers. A win there and +1000 in the NFC won’t last.

The market is treating Cousins like a stopgap. I’m treating him like the missing piece for the best defense in football.

Give me the Vikings to win the NFC (+1000).

title: Meghan's father Thomas Markle back in federal custody after allegedly removing ankle monitor
excerpt:
Thomas Markle was placed under house detention at his assisted living facility in Florida last week

Thomas Markle, the father of Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, is back in federal custody in Florida after...
body_text:
Thomas Markle was placed under house detention at his assisted living facility in Florida last week

Thomas Markle, the father of Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, is back in federal custody in Florida after allegedly removing his ankle monitor, according to court documents.

Markle appeared before a federal magistrate judge in the Florida city of Tampa on Tuesday and was denied bond. Prosecutors say he removed the monitor early that morning.

US Judge Lindsay S Griffin found on Tuesday that Markle had violated the conditions of his pretrial release, court documents show.

Markle, who has denied possessing images of child sex abuse, was arrested in Florida last week and placed under house detention. He was also ordered to wear a location monitoring device.

The BBC has contacted his representatives.

Griffin described Markle's housing situation as "untenable", writing in the order revoking his pretrial release that "based on the lack of suitable housing, no condition or combination of conditions would reasonably assure the safety of any other person or the community and the defendant's appearance in court".

He also ordered a medical evaluation for Markle and said he "must receive all necessary and prescribed medication unless discontinued by a physician".

"Release conditions are court orders, not suggestions," Bill Essayli, the US attorney for Central California, wrote on X on Tuesday.

"We will continue to prosecute this case to the fullest extent of the law," he added.

Markle, 82, was first arrested last week after the FBI, acting on warrants, searched storage units in Los Angeles registered to him which he had rented since 2008, with the last payment being made in October this year, the DoJ said.

Inside the units the FBI says agents seized about 78 items, including film negatives, slides and books that they allege contained child sex abuse material.

Witnesses "positively identified" Markle in two of the images believed to contain child sex abuse material.

In those images, the man pictured "appears to be in the age range of 30s to 40s", which suggests the alleged abuse dates back decades as Markle is currently 82 years old.

Markle appeared in court last week following his arrest. No plea was taken during the appearance, which set several conditions for his pretrial release, including that he be kept in home detention.

He is charged with one count of possessing indecent images of children, according to the DoJ.

FBI director Kash Patel said last week that Markle "allegedly targeted innocent children and sought to steal their innocence through his criminal actions".

Markle has called the allegations "sick lies".

He moved to the Philippines last year after he had a series of strokes, and lived in Cebu until May. He was reportedly learning to walk again in Florida after having his leg amputated.

The duchess has been estranged from her father since 2018. The BBC understands she broke contact with him last year, telling him she and the authorities knew he had abused young girls.

In a previously shared statement, Meghan confirmed the existence of the letter and wrote: "I am deeply distressed... my thoughts are with any children who may have been harmed."

She said she hoped it could be understood why she had largely cut off contact from her father and did "not allow him to have contact with our children".
